o: Vertical bars pair up (1st with 2nd, 3rd with 4th, ...); asterisks inside a pair are ignored. Equivalently, asterisks count only when an even number of bars has been seen so far. Example 1: bars split the string so only 'c**o' region's two asterisks... precisely, the counted ones are the two '*' outside bar pairs → 2. Example 3 gives 5.
k: Track bar parity: a toggling boolean flipped on each '|'; count '*' only when parity is 'outside'.
Equivalently, split on '|' and count asterisks in even-indexed chunks.

a.i: One pass with an `inside` flag: '|' flips it, '*' increments the answer only when the flag is false. This mirrors the pairing definition exactly.
s: For each char: '|' flips inside; '*' adds 1 to ans if not inside.

a.i: Splitting s on '|' yields chunks alternating outside/inside. Asterisks in chunks with even index (0-based) are counted; sum them.
a.t: O(|s|) — splitting and scanning each chunk once.

w: Both approaches are linear; the parity toggle avoids allocating substrings. Pitfall: assuming bars delimit 'comments' greedily beyond pairs — they strictly alternate. Empty chunks between adjacent bars are fine. Follow-up: nested or escaped bars would require a small state machine instead of a boolean.
